items.title: Arrival
items.pace: Land, get IC cards sorted, no fixed plans beyond dinner.
items.tldr: Land, sort out IC cards, and ease into Tokyo with a no-reservation conveyor-sushi dinner.
items.body: Get an IC card per person on arrival (Suica, PASMO, or a Tourist PASMO if landing at Narita) — everything else in this guide assumes you have one. Settle in, then keep dinner easy: Uobei Genki Sushi in Shibuya needs no reservation and moves fast even for a group of six, a forgiving first night after a long flight.

items.title: Asakusa, then the anchor dinner
items.pace: Easy morning, Asakusa mid-morning, a deliberately light afternoon before a serious dinner.
items.tldr: Senso-ji and Nakamise-dori in the morning, a light afternoon, then RyuGin — the trip's one splurge dinner.
items.body:
Senso-ji and Nakamise-dori make an easy, food-forward morning — snack your way down the approach street rather than committing to a sit-down lunch. Keep lunch light and the afternoon unstructured; tonight is the anchor.

Dinner is Nihonryori RyuGin in Hibiya (see Food & shopping) — book through your hotel concierge as soon as accommodation is confirmed, since October dates only opened Sept 1, 2026.
constraints: RyuGin reservation required — book via hotel concierge, see Food & shopping

items.title: Tsukiji, Harajuku, Shinjuku
items.pace: Early market morning, a shrine and a garden in the afternoon, dinner in Omoide Yokocho.
items.tldr: A grazing breakfast at Tsukiji, Meiji Jingu and Shinjuku Gyoen in the afternoon, dinner at a group-friendly Omoide Yokocho stall.
items.body:
Start at Tsukiji Outer Market before 9 AM — it gets genuinely crowded by mid-morning, and Toyosu (today being Sunday) is closed, so the outer market is the day's only market stop.

Meiji Jingu is calmest at 7 AM, which doesn't fit today's Tsukiji-first morning — expect more visitors than the guide's ideal, still worth the walk from Harajuku. Shinjuku Gyoen closes at 4:30 PM (last entry 4:00), so plan the afternoon around that.

Dinner is Torien in Omoide Yokocho — one of the few stalls there that actually books a group of six, rather than the 6-seat counters most of the alley runs on.

items.title: Toyosu and teamLab
items.pace: A bay-area morning, gallery midday, wagyu dinner back in Ginza.
items.tldr: Toyosu Market and teamLab Planets by day, a self-booked wagyu yakiniku dinner in Ginza at night.
items.body:
Toyosu Market is open today — browse rather than queue for Sushi Dai/Daiwa Sushi's counters (2–5 hour waits, and a party of six will likely be split in two). teamLab Planets is a few minutes away and fills the rest of the morning/early afternoon.

Shinjuku Gyoen is closed on Mondays, so it isn't on today's plan — that's already covered from Sunday.

Dinner is Yakiniku Ushigoro in Ginza, a short ride back from Toyosu — booked online, no concierge needed.

items.title: Yanaka and Ameyoko, then departure
items.pace: A relaxed morning food crawl, then the airport.
items.tldr: One last grazing morning through Yanaka Ginza and Ameyoko before heading to the airport.
items.body:
Yanaka Ginza (via Nippori Station) and Ameya-Yokocho (Ueno–Okachimachi) are a short hop apart and both work as pure grazing — no sit-down meal to plan around a flight. Ameyoko is calmest on a weekday morning, which this is.

Work backward from your flight using the airport transit times in the Transit tab — Haneda is faster to reach from central Tokyo than Narita if your return flight gives you the choice.
